# v1.1.0-dev.67 — Apply now can be undone

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.66`.

The open list from last release's research, worked through.

## Fifteen Seconds To Change Your Mind

A resolution change is the one setting that can leave you unable to
see the control you would use to undo it. That is why Windows gives
you fifteen seconds of Keep or Revert, why NVIDIA makes you confirm
after a test, why macOS counts down, and why CRU watches for F8.

WLM had none of it. **Apply now** arms a countdown:

```
Keep these display settings? Reverting in 12 seconds.
                              [Revert now]  [Keep these settings]
```

The timeout is the half that matters. It fires when the screen is
unreadable and no click is coming.

Your previous settings are captured before the change, from what
the editor already knows. Nothing extra is read. If a display's
scaling controls disagree with what Windows reports it is actually
running at, its scaling is left alone rather than restored to a
number WLM can't trust. Closing the editor cancels the countdown
rather than reverting your displays later with no explanation.

## "Windows Refused" Sometimes Meant "Saved"

When a display change needs a restart, Windows says so with its own
return code. The change **has** already been written. WLM reported
that as a refusal, which left a pending change unmentioned.

It now says the resolution is saved and will apply after a restart.

## 59 Hz Was Always 59.94 Hz

Windows reports the film and video rates as truncated whole numbers.
A 60 Hz monitor offers you "60" and "59" with nothing to distinguish
them. The second one is 59.94, the NTSC rate.

It says so now. Only when the whole number above it is also on offer
at that size, which is what makes it a pair rather than two
genuinely different rates.

## The Explanation Was Invisible To Screen Readers

The line under the resolution picker is the only place a rejected
size gets explained. It was plain text with no role. A screen reader
never read it out, and never re-read it when it changed.

It's announced now. The by-hand boxes point at it. The dropdowns and
number boxes have proper names instead of relying on their
placeholder text.

## One For The Changelog

While wiring the accessibility work, the by-hand boxes ended up
referring to the explanation line before it existed. In JavaScript
that throws rather than warns. The whole resolution picker would have
failed to open.

No unit test could have caught it, because the picker only exists
inside the running app. It was found by building one in a live
window and reading it back, which is now how this part of the UI
gets checked.

## Still Open

Two things did not make it. Rushing them after that near miss seemed
like a poor trade.

A saved size your display can't currently do is explained in a
sentence when it deserves a mark on the row itself.

And a third-party Parsec tool renumbers the driver's resolution
slots when it writes them, which can leave WLM treating another
app's resolutions as yours. Slot position turns out not to prove
ownership. The fix is a real design change rather than a patch.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
